topic: the Hiroshima 'human shadow' that's actually bleached stone, not a burn
title: Hiroshima's Famous 'Shadow' Isn't Actually a Burn Mark
description: AI-narrated commentary on the real science and history behind Hiroshima's 'human shadow' phenomenon: why the famous shadow etched in stone isn't actually a burn mark, but bleached stone around it. Educational history content with original commentary, not a reenactment or archival narration.

hook_candidates.text: Bleach marks everyone calls a nuclear shadow are actually the opposite of a burn.
A nuclear flash can bleach solid stone white in a fraction of a second.
What if that famous nuclear 'shadow' isn't a burn at all?
On August 6th, 1945, someone's outline was bleached into a bank's stone steps.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who thinks they already know everything about Hiroshima's shadow, because they want to prove that mark isn't even a burn.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume Hiroshima's nuclear shadow is a burn mark, but it's actually the opposite: bleached stone, not a scorch mark.
closing_comment: Hiroshima's famous 'shadow' isn't actually a burn mark, it's bleached stone, and it's still sitting inside a museum today.

sources.note: Confirms the Sumitomo Bank steps (~260m from hypocenter) were bleached white by thermal flash, leaving a dark shadow where a person blocked the rays.
Confirms the artifact was relocated to and remains preserved at the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum.
Confirms thermal radiation travels near light speed while the blast/shock wave arrives seconds later, far slower.
